reasoning: ث is t in Palestinian, so the word is respelled with ت. The dual ending is long ee; used in counting, as in تنتين ونص.
ق is a glottal stop. Literally 'may you bury me', an endearment heard across the Levant and most strongly associated with Lebanon; in Ramallah تسلم or يقبرني are at least as common.
إذا is said iza in Palestinian, so it is respelled with ز. Both initial hamzas sit on vowel seats and are not romanized.
shu is the Palestinian 'what'. b- plus yishtaghil contracts to bishtaghil, and أبو takes the 2ms suffix: abuuk.
The ص voices to z before the غ in Levantine speech, so this is said zghiir; the spelling is kept because the emphasis is still there for some speakers (Sghiir). علي with the doubled y is 'on me'.
ص is emphatic S; taa marbuta after م is e. Used of a thumbprint and of a fingerprint scanner at work.
Urban Palestinian has no interdental ظ: it falls together with ض, so this is said 7aDD with a doubled emphatic. The spelling حظ is kept because it is the established form of the word.
ض is emphatic D and the taa marbuta after ل is e. Plural 3aDalaat.
Quadriliteral form from the loan 'nerves', with the Palestinian mit- participle prefix. Everyday Ramallah word.
Plural of قيمة; ق glottalises as in the singular 'iime. Careful or formal speech may keep [q] here.
Form II optative with no b- prefix; the short vowel after the doubled ل drops before the suffix, giving ysallmak. Standard reply to الله يعطيك العافية.
The -iyya suffix is -iyye with shadda on the ي. In Palestinian it is the ordinary word for a surgical operation.

ما negates the verb kaan, as Palestinian requires. il-mafruuD with emphatic D is the standard 'supposed to', followed by a bare imperfect.
ثانية is taanye in Palestinian, respelled with ت, with the medial vowel dropped. It means both 'another time' and 'again'.
Form VI with the Palestinian it- prefix and emphatic S: itSaala7 ma3o 'he made up with him'.
Long ee, with the initial hamza on a vowel seat and so not romanized. It is used in southern Palestine, Jordan and Egypt; a Ramallah speaker says shu.
khams plus miyye compounded into one word, with the doubled y of miyye and the final e.

Verbless sentence with the noun 7arr 'heat', doubled r from the shadda. ي is a moon letter.
